topic: Born-Wolf cosine-fourth natural optical vignetting vs quadratic Taylor corner blackout rig
topic_zh: Born-Wolf 物理余弦四次方自然镜头渐晕对比朴素二次泰勒抛物线广角死黑
scope: Deterministic Max Born & Emil Wolf / Kang & Weiss (CVPR 2000) rational root-free cosine-fourth natural vignetting (V(r, f) = cos^4(theta) = 1 / (1 + (r/f)^2)^2) versus naive second-order Taylor polynomial vignetting (max(0, 1 - 2*(r/f)^2)) and 64-ring exit-pupil trigonometric solid-angle integration across 17 sensor radial stations (u = r/f in [0.00, 1.00]). No neural lens emulation execution.

protocol.function: V_phys(r, f) = cos⁴θ ≡ 1 / (1 + (r / f)²)² → Station-12 (r/f=0.75) V = 0.4096 (0.0000 Corner Blackout)

robustness.name: Sampled 17 sensor radial stations preserve strictly positive physical cos^4(theta) illumination without corner blackout

good_fit: Physically Based Camera (PBC) post-processing in UE5, Unity HDRP, Frostbite, and Three.js virtual cinematography
Coupling lens vignetting automatically to dynamic focal-length zooming (24mm wide-angle naturally vignettes more than 85mm telephoto)
Evaluating cos⁴θ = 1 / (1 + (r/f)²)² in 3 rational ALU operations with zero sqrt(), atan(), or cos() calls
Applying vignetting in linear scene-referred radiance space prior to AgX tone mapping (Round 48) and sub-LSB dithering (Round 92)
not_for: Mechanical lens-hood occlusion (Mechanical Vignetting) where physical barrel clipping intentionally cuts a hard circular mask
Orthographic projection cameras where off-axis angle θ ≡ 0° everywhere
UI overlay canvases that should remain at uniform 100% brightness
